issue.title: Command Log Showing Object{11} when you pass {force: false} to .click()

labels.name: type: duplicate

issue.body:

### Current behavior:

```javascript
Cypress.Commands.add('dropdownSelectByText', (selector, text = '', force = false) => {
  cy.get(selector).click({ force: force });
  cy.contains('some-other-selector', text).click({ force: true});
]});
```
This is the result of calling that method with force = false.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10161067/49042504-1d683080-f1a7-11e8-9777-882be203b9ee.png)

After some digging I can say that this happens when you pass { force: false } to the .click() method, which is the default value for `force`

### Desired behavior:

Even if you are passing an option, with the default value we could just ignore it, or show the actual value you are passing. I think ignoring it, or displaying some hint text would be great.
Having an Object{11} is really misleading.

### Steps to reproduce:

call `.click({ force: false })`
I haven't tested the defaults for other commands, but it could be happening.

The issue seems to be around here https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/dd56faf97ad6e4713e785c0bf800f3a1463d7a1a/packages/driver/src/cypress/utils.coffee#L140

issue.title: Pass custom headers when clicking

labels.name: type: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

repository.name: cypress
repository.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

issue.body:
### Current behavior:

When custom `headers` are added to `cy.visit` they are properly added to the request. When executing a `cy.click` operation, the headers are not added to the result request.

### Desired behavior:

The `cy.click` sends the same request `headers` as `cy.visit` does.

### Versions

3.3.1
